context.answer: Program Kit 0.14.2; Foundation 0.3.6, Build 0.3.2, exporter 0.2.7, CShells 0.0.31, Forms 0.2.1, Localization 0.1.2. US1 human review of a policy workspace. Trigger: native browser sign-out to /auth/signed-out. Working tree has uncommitted fresh consumer implementation; only this bounded observation and selected publisher contract are included.

decision.answer: Retain the selected native authentication, session and presentation mechanism. Report the observable locale discontinuity and missing logo seam upstream; do not infer a maintainer decision. Consumer language/theme selection remains separate from the anonymous publisher page.

expectation.answer: Human review expects a Dutch-selected application to keep Dutch copy on signed-out pages and show product branding. Captured Presentation.Locale=nl and Web.DefaultLocale=nl establish declared locale; the complete publisher contract has Copy and colour presets but no logo seam. Automatic translated copy and application-language propagation are requested capabilities, not promises established by that contract.

lesson.answer: Proposed upstream assessment: add locale-aware defaults and a documented selected-language path, plus a constrained safe product-brand/logo contribution for anonymous authentication pages. Preserve native security/session behavior. This is a consumer observation and capability proposal, not an accepted repair.

observation.answer: Actual Chromium sign-in and native sign-out with a synthetic account and Dutch browser locale rendered html lang=nl, English Session status / No local session is active / Sign in / Return to application, and zero image elements. App name and green colours appeared.

remedy.answer: No signed-out workaround applied. The existing native anonymous landing remains selected. Separate consumer CSS changes address settings overflow and Keycloak input-frame appearance and do not repair this publisher-page locale/branding gap.

resources.answer: Consulted installed repair-request and implement skills, repair-feedback contract/operating procedure, actual Foundation settings contract and native browser/session configuration. Executed the prepared Playwright Chromium runtime and read the public landing. Bounded open/closed upstream issue searches found no candidates; this is not proof of uniqueness.

results.answer: The public-page observation was independently executed. Captured contract fields were inspected. Existing earlier US1 engineering passes do not prove localization or branding. Newer publisher versions, production/provider-wide behavior and maintainer diagnosis are unknown. Native sign-out completed and the public page reported no active local session.
